nodes.era: 1st c. CE (Cave of Treasures pp. 208-209; Book of the Bee Ch. 39)
nodes.role: Persian & Sabaean Royal Astronomers Following Nimrod's Prophecy to Christ
nodes.notes: Three kings: Hôrmîzdâdh of Mâkhôzdî (King of Kings of Persia), Îzgarad (Yazdegerd, King of Sâbhâ), and Perôzadh (King of Sheba). Book of the Bee expands to 12 named Magi with patronymics (Zarwândâd s/o Artabân, Gûshnâsâph s/o Gûndaphar [Indo-Parthian Gondophares!], Arshakh, Merôdâch, etc.)!

nodes.name: First Temple High Priests (Dutripon p. 23, #4–34): Abishua → Bukki → Uzzi → Zadok → Ahimaaz → Jehoiada → Hilkiah → Seraiah
nodes.role: Complete Pre-Exilic High Priestly Succession from Aaron to the Babylonian Exile
nodes.notes: Dutripon's Tabula Pontificum apud Judaeos harmonizes Chronicles, Josephus & Eusebius across all 34 pre-exilic High Priests, including Jehoiada (who sheltered young King Joash from Queen Athaliah) and Hilkiah (who discovered the Book of the Law under King Josiah).

nodes.name: Herodian & Roman-Era High Priests (Dutripon p. 23, #63–91): Ananelus → Simon ben Boethus → Annas (Ananus) → Joseph Caiaphas → Ananias ben Nebedeus → Ananus II → Phannias (70 CE)
nodes.era: 37 BCE – 70 CE (Dutripon Concordantiae p. 23; Gospels; Acts 23; Josephus Ant. XV-XX)
nodes.role: Complete Final 29 High Priests of the Second Temple Down to the Fall of Jerusalem (70 CE)
nodes.notes: Complete chronological table from Herod's appointee Ananelus & Simon ben Boethus (Herod's father-in-law) through Annas (Ananus) and son-in-law Joseph Caiaphas (Trial of Jesus), Annas's 5 High Priest sons (Eleazar, Jonathan, Theophilus, Matthias, Ananus II — who executed James the Just in 62 CE!), Ananias ben Nebedeus (Trial of Paul, Acts 23), down to Phannias/Phanacius, the VERY LAST High Priest chosen by lot during the 70 CE siege!

nodes.name: 11 Territorial Dukes of Esau (Timna, Alvah, Jetheth, Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon, Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar, Magdiel, Iram) & Jobab = Job Bridge
nodes.role: Final Edomite Chiefs & Septuagint/Vulgate Identification of King Jobab with Patriarch Job
nodes.notes: Dutripon's Series Principum Regumque Idumaeorum explicitly records the ancient Septuagint/Vulgate tradition ('Jobab iste est Job speculum patientiae') identifying Edomite King #2 Jobab ben Zerah of Bozrah with the Biblical Patriarch Job, followed by the 11 territorial Dukes of Edom.

nodes.name: Deuterocanonical & Vulgate Households (Dutripon pp. 10-15): Tobit & Tobias (+ Sarah bat Raguel), Judith of Bethulia, Susanna, Eleazar & 7 Maccabean Martyrs, Ben Sira & Prophetesses Huldah & Anna
nodes.era: c. 744 BCE – 1 CE (Dutripon Index Chronologicus pp. 10-15)
nodes.role: Biblical & Intertestamental Families Preserved in the Latin Vulgate Chronology
sources: Books of Tobit, Judith, Sirach, 2 Maccabees
nodes.notes: Tobit (Tribe of Naphtali, exiled to Nineveh under Shalmaneser) -> Tobias (+ Sarah daughter of Raguel); Widow Judith of Bethulia (slew General Holofernes); Susanna (vindicated by Daniel); Eleazar & 7 Maccabean Martyrs (168 BCE); Jesus ben Sirach (Sirach/Ecclesiasticus, translated in Alexandria 131 BCE); Prophetess Huldah (Josiah's reign) & Prophetess Anna bat Phanuel (Tribe of Asher, Temple of Jerusalem!).

nodes.name: Intersecting Ancient Near Eastern Kings in Dutripon's Sacred Chronology (pp. 9-14): Chedorlaomer of Elam, Sihon & Og of Bashan, Cushan-Rishathaim, Eglon of Moab, Jabin & Sisera, Zerah the Cushite & Tibni
nodes.era: c. 1949-880 BCE (Dutripon pp. 9-14; Gen 14; Num 21; Judges 3-4; 2 Chr 14)
nodes.role: Foreign Kings & Rivals Synchronized Across Dutripon's Six Ages of the World
nodes.notes: Key intersecting monarchs in Dutripon's Six Ages tables: Chedorlaomer of Elam (vs. Abraham, Gen 14), Amorite Kings Sihon & Og of Bashan (Num 21), Cushan-Rishathaim of Aram-Naharaim (vs. Othniel), Eglon of Moab (vs. Ehud), Jabin of Hazor & Sisera (vs. Deborah/Barak), Zerah the Cushite/Ethiopian (vs. King Asa, 2 Chr 14), and rival King Tibni of Israel (vs. Omri, 1 Kgs 16).

nodes.name: Dutripon's Vulgate Ethnographic & Onomastic Key (pp. 9-15, 24-26): Nimrod=Belus, Asshur=Ninus, Armenia=Ararat, Carthago=Tarshish, India=Ophir/Hodu, Greece=Javan, Libya=Lubim & Patriarch Etymologies
nodes.role: Classical Latin Vulgate Cross-Cultural Identifications & Hebrew/Chaldean/Greek Name Meanings

nodes.name: 1. Tudiya (1st Assyrian Tent-King)
nodes.role: First King of Assyria (Ebla Treaty Attested!)
nodes.notes: First of the '17 kings who lived in tents' in the Assyrian King List; historically attested in the Ebla archives concluding a trade treaty with Vizier Ibrium of Ebla!

nodes.name: 2. Adamu (2nd Assyrian Tent-King)
nodes.notes: Second king of Assyria in the AKL; earliest known historical ruler bearing the Semitic name Adamu ('Man/Red Earth'), cognate with Biblical Adam!

nodes.name: 3–8. Yangi, Suhlamu, Harharu, Mandaru, Imsu & Harsu
nodes.notes: Kings 3-8 of the AKL tent-dwellers, reflecting Amorite/West Semitic pastoral confederacies.

nodes.name: 9–10. Didanu (Tidnum) & Hanu (Hana)
nodes.notes: Didanu corresponds to the Amorite tribe Tidnum/Ditanu (also ancestral to the Ugaritic royal cult and compared with Biblical Dedan); Hanu corresponds to the Middle Euphrates tribe of Hana.

nodes.name: 11–15. Zuabu, Nuabu, Abazu, Belu & Azarah
nodes.notes: Kings 11-15 of the canonical Assyrian King List (Pruzsinszky Table 17a).

nodes.name: 16. Ushpia (Builder of the Temple of Ashur)
nodes.role: Founder of the E-hursag-kurkurra Temple of Ashur
nodes.notes: Credited in inscriptions of Shalmaneser I and Esarhaddon as the earliest founder of the great Temple of the god Ashur in Assur.

nodes.name: 17. Apiashal (Son of Ushpia — Bridge to Ancestors)
nodes.role: Last Tent-King & First of the 10 Ancestors
nodes.notes: Appears at both the end of Section 1 (17 tent-dwellers) and the beginning of Section 2 (10 kings whose fathers are known), linking Shamshi-Adad I's pedigree back to Ushpia!

nodes.name: 18–24. Hale, Samani, Hayani, Ilu-Mer, Yakmesi, Yakmeni & Yazkur-El
nodes.notes: Listed in reverse genealogical order ('PN1 son of PN2') in AKL Section 2 to trace the Amorite royal pedigree of Shamshi-Adad I (Pruzsinszky pp. 48, 51).

nodes.name: 25–26. Ilu-kabkabi & Aminu (Father & Brother of Shamshi-Adad I)
nodes.notes: Ilu-kabkabi fathered Aminu and the great conqueror Shamshi-Adad I.

nodes.name: 27–29. Sulili, Kikia & Akia (End of Ur III Period)
nodes.role: Early City-Rulers of Assur (Wall Builder Kikia)
nodes.notes: Kikia built the city wall of Assur; Sulili (son of Aminu) marks Assur's independence after Ur III.

nodes.name: 30–32. Puzur-Ashur I → Shalim-ahum → Ilushuma
nodes.role: Founders of the Old Assyrian Merchant Dynasty
nodes.notes: Ilushuma established free trade privileges for Akkadian merchants and founded the Old Assyrian trading empire.

nodes.name: 33–34. Erishum I (40 yrs, First Eponym List!) → Ikunum (15 yrs)
nodes.role: First King with Kültepe Eponym List (līmu) Chronology
nodes.notes: Erishum I rebuilt the Ashur Temple and inaugurated the Kültepe Eponym List (KEL), giving exact year-by-year dating from 1974/1934 BCE!

nodes.name: 35–38. Sargon I (40 yrs) → Puzur-Ashur II → Naram-Sin of Assur → Erishum II
nodes.role: Height of Old Assyrian Anatolian Colony Trade (Kanesh)
nodes.notes: Named after the great Akkadian kings Sargon & Naram-Sin; overthrown in 1808 BCE by Shamshi-Adad I.

nodes.name: 39–40. Shamshi-Adad I (33 yrs) → Ishme-Dagan I (40 yrs) & Yasmah-Adad
nodes.role: Founder of the Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia (Contemporary of Hammurabi!)
nodes.notes: Son of Ilu-kabkabi; conquered Assur, Mari, and Shubat-Enlil. His son Ishme-Dagan I ruled Ekallatum/Assur while Yasmah-Adad ruled Mari (famed in the Mari Letters!).

nodes.name: 41–47. Ashur-dugul & Six Usurpers (Ashur-apla-idi, Nasir-Sin, Sin-namir, Ipqi-Ishtar, Adad-salulu, Adasi)
nodes.role: Interregnum & Adasi (Progenitor of the 1,000-Year Adaside Dynasty!)
nodes.notes: Six 'sons of a nobody' ruled briefly; the last, Adasi, became the revered ancestor of Assyria's royal Adaside house down to Esarhaddon!

nodes.name: 48–53. Belu-bani (son of Adasi) → Libaya → Sharma-Adad I → Iptar-Sin → Bazaya → Lullaya
nodes.notes: Belu-bani (10 yrs) founded the unbroken Adaside royal dynasty; Bazaya ruled 28 years.

nodes.name: 54–66. Kidin-Ninua → Sharma-Adad II → Erishum III → Shamshi-Adad II → Ishme-Dagan II → Shamshi-Adad III → Ashur-nirari I → Puzur-Ashur III → Enlil-nasir I → Nur-ili → Ashur-shaduni → Ashur-rabi I → Ashur-nadin-ahhe I
nodes.role: Late Old Assyrian / Mitanni Vassalage Kings
nodes.notes: Preserved unbroken Adaside patrilineal continuity through the Mitanni era (Pruzsinszky Table 17b).

nodes.name: 67–72. Enlil-nasir II → Ashur-nirari II → Ashur-bel-nisheshu → Ashur-rim-nisheshu → Ashur-nadin-ahhe II → Eriba-Adad I
nodes.notes: Eriba-Adad I (27 yrs) broke Mitanni supremacy, setting the stage for his son Ashur-uballit I.

nodes.name: 73–76. Ashur-uballit I (Amarna Letters!) → Enlil-nirari → Arik-den-ili → Adad-nirari I
nodes.role: Founders of the Middle Assyrian Great Power
nodes.notes: Ashur-uballit I (36 yrs) wrote directly to Pharaoh Akhenaten as 'Great King' (EA 15-16) and married his daughter Muballitat-Sherua to Kassite Babylon! Adad-nirari I (32 yrs) annexed Hanigalbat (Mitanni).

nodes.name: 77–78. Shalmaneser I (30 yrs) → Tukulti-Ninurta I (37 yrs, Conqueror of Babylon)
nodes.role: Peak of the Middle Assyrian Empire
nodes.notes: Shalmaneser I founded Kalhu (Nimrud); Tukulti-Ninurta I captured Kassite King Kashtiliash IV of Babylon and built Kar-Tukulti-Ninurta — often compared with the Nimrod legend!

nodes.name: 79–86. Ashur-nadin-apli → Ashur-nirari III → Enlil-kudurri-usur → Ninurta-apil-Ekur → Ashur-dan I (46 yrs) → Ninurta-tukulti-Ashur → Mutakkil-Nusku → Ashur-resh-ishi I
nodes.notes: Ninurta-apil-Ekur (descendant of Eriba-Adad I) restored dynastic stability; Ashur-dan I ruled 46 years; Ashur-resh-ishi I defeated Nebuchadnezzar I of Babylon.

nodes.name: 87–97. Tiglath-Pileser I (39 yrs) → Ashared-apil-Ekur → Ashur-bel-kala → Eriba-Adad II → Shamshi-Adad IV → Ashurnasirpal I → Shalmaneser II → Ashur-nirari IV → Ashur-rabi II (41 yrs) → Ashur-resh-ishi II → Tiglath-Pileser II
nodes.role: Tiglath-Pileser I's Mediterranean Campaigns & Aramean Era
nodes.notes: Tiglath-Pileser I marched to the Mediterranean, hunted elephants in Syria, and compiled the Middle Assyrian Laws. Followed by 140 years of Aramean pressure until Ashur-dan II.

nodes.name: 98–101. Ashur-dan II → Adad-nirari II → Tukulti-Ninurta II → Ashurnasirpal II (Nimrud Palace)
nodes.notes: Adad-nirari II inaugurated the unbroken Eponym Canon (911-649 BCE); Ashurnasirpal II (25 yrs) built the magnificent Northwest Palace at Kalhu (Nimrud).

nodes.name: 102. Shalmaneser III (35 yrs — Black Obelisk of Jehu & Battle of Qarqar!)
nodes.role: First Assyrian King Explicitly Naming Israelite Kings Ahab & Jehu
nodes.notes: Fought King Ahab of Israel & Hadadezer of Damascus at Qarqar (853 BCE); his Black Obelisk depicts King Jehu of Israel ('son of Omri') bowing in tribute — the ONLY contemporary depiction of an Israelite king!

nodes.name: 103–104. Shamshi-Adad V & Queen Shammuramat (Semiramis!) → Adad-nirari III
nodes.role: Historical Queen Semiramis & Adad-nirari III (Tribute of Joash of Israel)
nodes.notes: Babylonian princess Shammuramat (Greek: Semiramis!) served as regent/queen mother alongside her son Adad-nirari III (28 yrs), who collected tribute from Jehoash of Israel and Ben-Hadad of Damascus.

nodes.name: 105–107. Shalmaneser IV → Ashur-dan III (763 BCE Bur-Sagale Solar Eclipse!) → Ashur-nirari V
nodes.role: Anchor of All Ancient Near Eastern Chronology (June 15, 763 BCE Eclipse)
nodes.notes: The Assyrian Eponym List records a total solar eclipse in Sivan under Ashur-dan III (June 15, 763 BCE), astronomically locking ALL Assyrian and Biblical monarchic dates!

nodes.name: 108–109. Tiglath-Pileser III (Pul, 745-727 BCE) → Shalmaneser V (726-722 BCE, Siege of Samaria)
nodes.role: Final Kings of Canonical AKL (SDAS Tablet) & Biblical 'Pul'
nodes.notes: Tiglath-Pileser III (called 'Pul' in 2 Kings 15:19) created the provincial empire; his son Shalmaneser V besieged Samaria (final king on the SDAS AKL tablet!).

nodes.name: 110–116. Sargonid Dynasty: Sargon II → Sennacherib → Esarhaddon → Ashurbanipal → Ashur-etil-ilani → Sin-shar-ishkun → Ashur-uballit II
nodes.role: Final Imperial Dynasty of Nineveh (Library of Ashurbanipal)
nodes.notes: Sargon II completed the conquest of Israel (722 BCE); Sennacherib besieged Hezekiah's Jerusalem (701 BCE); Esarhaddon conquered Egypt (671 BCE); Ashurbanipal built the great Library of Nineveh (preserving Gilgamesh!). Fell to Babylon & Media in 612-609 BCE.

nodes.name: Ur I Dynasty: Mesannepada → Aannepada → Meskiagnunna → Elulu → Balulu
nodes.era: c. 2560-2400 BCE (SKL Col. iii-iv, Jacobsen pp. 93-95)
nodes.role: First Dynasty of Ur (Royal Tombs of Ur Era)
nodes.notes: 5 kings (177 yrs): Mesannepada -> son Aannepada (restored from Tummal Chronicle & inscriptions!) -> Meskiagnunna -> Elulu -> Balulu.

nodes.name: Awan (3 Kings), Kish II (8 Kings: Susuda, Dadasig, Magalgalla, Kalbum, Tuge, Enbi-Ishtar, Lugalmu) & Hamazi (Hatanish)
nodes.era: c. 2500-2400 BCE (SKL Col. iv, Jacobsen pp. 95-99)
nodes.role: Early Dynastic Hegemonies of Elam, Kish & Zagros
nodes.notes: Awan (Elamite dynasty, 3 kings, 356 yrs), Kish II (8 kings incl. Kalbum son of Magalgalla), and Hamazi (King Hatanish, later deified in god-list AN:Anum!).

nodes.name: Uruk II (Enshakushanna, Lugal-kinishe-dudu, Lugal-kisal-si), Ur II (Kaku), Adab (Lugal-annemundu) & Mari (Ansud)
nodes.era: c. 2450-2350 BCE (SKL Col. iv-v, Jacobsen pp. 100-103)
nodes.notes: Enshakushanna of Uruk; Lugal-kinishe-dudu & son Lugal-kisal-si (ruled both Uruk II & Ur II!); Lugal-annemundu of Adab (90 yrs, legendary conqueror from Elam to Cedar Mountain); Ansud & 5 kings of Mari.

nodes.name: Queen Ku-Baba (Kish III — Sole Female Monarch in the Sumerian King List!)
nodes.era: c. 2400 BCE (SKL Col. v 36-41, Jacobsen pp. 104-105)
nodes.role: Tavern-Keeper Who Consolidated Kish & Founded Kish III–IV
nodes.notes: Ku(g)-Baba ('Baba-ellit', former alewife/barmaid, reigned 100 yrs) is the ONLY woman listed as sovereign king in the entire Sumerian King List; mother of Puzur-Sin & grandmother of Ur-Zababa!

nodes.name: Akshak (Unzi, Undalulu, Ur-ur, Puzur-Nirah, Ishu-il, Shu-Sin) & Kish IV (Puzur-Sin → Ur-Zababa → Simu-dar → Usi-watar → Eshtar-muti → Ishme-Shamash → Nannia)
nodes.era: c. 2400-2334 BCE (SKL Col. v-vi, Jacobsen pp. 106-111)
nodes.role: Dynasty of Ku-Baba's Descendants & Master of Young Sargon
nodes.notes: Ku-Baba's son Puzur-Sin -> son Ur-Zababa of Kish, whose royal cupbearer was Sargon of Akkad! Contemporary with Akshak's 6 kings.

nodes.name: Uruk III: Lugal-zagesi (25 yrs — First Unifier of Sumer Before Sargon)
nodes.era: c. 2359-2335 BCE (SKL Col. vi 24-27, Jacobsen pp. 110-111)
nodes.role: Ensi of Umma & Sole King of Uruk III
nodes.notes: United all of Sumer from the Lower Sea (Persian Gulf) to the Upper Sea (Mediterranean) before being defeated and led in a neck-stock to Nippur by Sargon of Akkad.

nodes.name: Late Akkad Interregnum (Igigi, Nanum, Imi, Elulu) → Dudu → Shu-Durul
nodes.era: c. 2193-2154 BCE (SKL Col. vii 1-12, Jacobsen pp. 114-115)
nodes.role: Final Rulers of the Sargonic Akkadian Empire
nodes.notes: 'Who was king? Who was not king?' Four rival claimants reigned 3 years before Dudu (21 yrs) and his son Shu-Durul (15 yrs) closed the Dynasty of Agade.

nodes.name: Uruk IV (Ur-nigin → Ur-gigir → Kudda → Puzur-ili → Ur-Utu), 21 Gutian Kings (Erridupizir to Tirigan) & Uruk V (Utu-hegal)
nodes.era: c. 2154-2112 BCE (SKL Col. vii-viii, Jacobsen pp. 114-123)
nodes.role: Gutian Domination & Sumerian Liberation by Utu-hegal
nodes.notes: 21 Gutian rulers from the Zagros mountains (Erridupizir, Imta, Inkishush, Sarlagab, Iarlagab, Hablum -> Puzur-Sin, Si'um, Tirigan [40 days]) expelled by Utu-hegal of Uruk V — whose general/relative Ur-Nammu founded Ur III!

nodes.name: Independent Lagash II: Ur-Nanshe → Eannatum (Stele of Vultures) → Urukagina → Gudea of Lagash
nodes.notes: Omitted from the partisan SKL: Ur-Nanshe, Eannatum, law-reformer Urukagina (oldest legal code against corruption), and pious Ensi Gudea of Lagash (contemporary of Ur-Nammu).

nodes.name: Isin I Dynasty (All 15 Kings): Ishbi-Erra → Shu-ilishu → Iddin-Dagan → Ishme-Dagan → Lipit-Ishtar → Ur-Ninurta → Bur-Sin → Lipit-Enlil → Erra-imitti → Enlil-bani → Zambia → Iter-pisha → Ur-dukuga → Sin-magir → Damiq-ilishu
nodes.era: c. 2017-1794 BCE (SKL Col. viii 23-45, Jacobsen pp. 124-127)
nodes.role: Final Dynasty of the Sumerian King List (Code of Lipit-Ishtar)
nodes.notes: Ishbi-Erra broke away from Ibbi-Sin of Ur III. Lipit-Ishtar issued the Sumerian Law Code (180 yrs before Hammurabi!). Gardener Enlil-bani succeeded Erra-imitti (substitute-king ritual!). Ended when Rim-Sin of Larsa conquered Damiq-ilishu.

nodes.name: Babylon I (All 11 Amorite Kings): Sumu-abum → Sumu-la-El → Sabium → Apil-Sin → Sin-muballit → Hammurabi → Samsu-iluna → Abi-eshuh → Ammi-ditana → Ammi-saduqa → Samsu-ditana
nodes.role: Complete Old Babylonian Amorite Dynasty (Venus Tablet of Ammi-saduqa!)
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: Sumu-abum (contemporary of Ilushuma of Assyria) -> Hammurabi (defeated Rim-Sin of Larsa, son of Kudur-Mabuk!) -> son Samsu-iluna -> Abi-eshuh -> Ammi-ditana -> Ammi-saduqa (astronomical Venus Tablet!) -> Samsu-ditana (overthrown by Hittite King Mursili I in 1595 BCE!).

nodes.name: Babylon II (First Sealand Dynasty, All 11 Kings): Iluma-ilu → Itti-ili-nibi → Damqi-ilishu → Ishkibal → Shushshi → Gulkishar → Peshgaldaramesh → Ayadaragalama → Akurduana → Melamkurkurra → Ea-gamil
nodes.role: Southern Marshland Dynasty Overlapping Babylon I & Kassites
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: Iluma-ilu fought Samsu-iluna & Abi-eshuh; Gulkishar anchored Babylonian chronology (696 yrs before Nebuchadnezzar I); last king Ea-gamil invaded Elam and was overthrown by Kassite Ulam-Buriash!

nodes.name: Babylon III (Kassite Dynasty, 576 yrs): Gandash → Agum I → Kashtiliash I → Agum II (Restored Marduk!) → Burna-Buriash I → Ulam-Buriash → Burna-Buriash II (Amarna Letters!) → Kurigalzu → Kudur-Enlil → Shagarakti-Shuriash → Meli-Shipak
nodes.role: Longest-Reigning Dynasty in Babylonian History (Zagros Mountain Origin)
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: Agum II (son of Urzigurumash) retrieved Marduk's statue from Hani; Ulam-Buriash conquered the Sealand; Burna-Buriash II corresponded with Akhenaten & married Ashur-uballit I's daughter!

nodes.name: Babylon IV (Isin II): Nebuchadnezzar I → Enlil-nadin-apli → Marduk-nadin-ahhe → Marduk-shapik-zeri → Adad-apla-iddina
nodes.role: Revival of Native Babylon & Recovery of Marduk from Elam
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: Nebuchadnezzar I sacked Susa in Elam and restored Marduk to Babylon; Adad-apla-iddina (Aramean/son of Itti-Marduk-balatu) married his daughter to Assyrian King Ashur-bel-kala.

nodes.name: Babylon V–IX: 2nd Sealand (Simbar-Shipak), Bazi Dynasty, Elamite Mar-biti-apla-usur, Nabu-mukin-apli, Nabonassar (747 BCE Era!) & Merodach-Baladan II
nodes.era: 1025-626 BCE (L.W. King Vol. I pp. 184-208; Eusebius)
nodes.role: Ptolemaic Astronomical Era of Nabonassar & Chaldean Resistance
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: King Nabonassar (747 BCE) inaugurated the famous Babylonian astronomical diaries & Ptolemy's Almagest Canon! Chaldean hero Merodach-Baladan II (Marduk-apla-iddina II) sent envoys to King Hezekiah of Judah (2 Kgs 20:12) against Assyria.

nodes.name: Babylon X (Neo-Babylonian / Chaldean Empire): Nabopolassar → Nebuchadnezzar II → Amel-Marduk (Evil-Merodach) → Neriglissar → Labashi-Marduk → Nabonidus & Crown Prince Belshazzar
nodes.role: Final Native Babylonian Empire (Hanging Gardens & Fall to Cyrus, 539 BCE)
sources: Early Babylonian Chronicles (L.W. King Vol. I)
nodes.notes: Nabopolassar allied with Cyaxares of Media to destroy Nineveh (612 BCE); Nebuchadnezzar II built Babylon's Ishtar Gate & exiled Judah (586 BCE); Nabonidus (+ Queen Nitocris / Adad-guppi) & son Belshazzar fell to Cyrus the Great in 539 BCE!

nodes.name: Manetho's Pre-Dynastic Rulers: Gods (Ptah→Re→Shu→Geb→Osiris→Seth→Horus), Demigods & Shemsu-Hor ('Spirits of the Dead')
nodes.era: Predynastic Mythic Era (Manetho Fr. 1-4, Loeb pp. 3-19)
nodes.role: 24,900 Lunar Years of Divine & Demigod Kingship Before Menes
nodes.notes: Manetho's opening sequence: 6 Great Gods (Hephaestus/Ptah -> son Helios/Re -> Agathodaemon/Shu -> Cronos/Geb -> Osiris & Isis -> Typhon/Seth), 9 Demigods (Horus, Ares/Anhur, Anubis, Heracles/Khonsu, Apollo, Ammon, Tithoes, Sosus, Zeus), down to Bydis/Bites and the Shemsu-Hor ('Followers of Horus / Spirits of the Dead').

nodes.name: Palermo Stone Predynastic Kings of Lower Egypt (Seka, Khayu, Tiu, Thesh, Neheb, Wazner, Mekh) & King Scorpion
nodes.role: Earliest Historically Inscribed Rulers of the Nile Before Narmer
nodes.notes: Row 1 of the 5th-Dynasty Palermo Stone preserves actual names of Pre-Unification Red Crown Kings of Lower Egypt: Seka, Khayu, Teyew/Tiu, Thesh, Neheb, Wazenez/Wazner, and Mekh — alongside Upper Egyptian Dynasty 0 rulers Iry-Hor, Ka, and King Scorpion.

nodes.name: Dynasty I Complete (Thinite, 8 Kings): Narmer/Menes → Hor-Aha (Athothis) → Djer (Kenkenes) → Djet (Uenephes) → Queen Merneith → Den (Usaphais) → Adjib (Miebis) → Semerkhet (Semempses) → Qa'a (Bieneches)
nodes.role: Complete Unification Dynasty (Africanus Makes Every King Son of His Predecessor)
nodes.notes: 179 historical years (Manetho: 253 yrs). Queen Merneith ruled as regent/mother of Den. Every Abydos royal tomb and Horus-name matched with Manetho's Greek names.

nodes.name: Dynasty II Complete (9 Kings): Hotepsekhemwy (Boethos) → Nebre (Kaiechos) → Nynetjer (Binothris) → Weneg (Tlas) → Sened (Sethenes) → Sneferka → Sekhemib → Seth-Peribsen (Sesochris) → Khasekhemwy (Cheneres)
nodes.notes: Manetho notes under Nynetjer (Binothris) it was decreed that women could hold the royal dignity; Peribsen took a Seth-name before Khasekhemwy united both Horus and Seth above his serekh!

nodes.name: Dynasty III Complete (Memphite, 5 Kings): Sanakht (Necherophes) → Netjerykhet/Djoser (Tosorthros + Imhotep) → Sekhemkhet (Tyris) → Khaba → Huni (Kerpheres)
nodes.role: Dawn of Stone Pyramid Architecture (Saqqara Step Pyramid)
nodes.notes: Djoser & architect Imhotep (Greek: Imuthes/Asclepius) built the first monumental stone pyramid; Huni inaugurated the royal cartouche.

nodes.name: Dynasty IV Complete (Pyramid Builders, 7 Kings): Sneferu (Soris) → Khufu (Suphis I) → Djedefre (Ratoises) → Khafre (Suphis II) → Baka (Bicheris) → Menkaure (Mencheres) → Shepseskaf (Sebercheres) & Queen Khentkawes
nodes.role: Complete Great Pyramid Dynasty of Dahshur & Giza
nodes.notes: Sneferu built 3 giant pyramids; sons/grandsons Khufu, Djedefre, Khafre, and Menkaure erected Giza; Menkaure's daughter Queen Khentkawes bridged Dynasties IV and V!

nodes.name: Dynasty V Complete (Solar Kings, 9 Kings): Userkaf (Usercheres) → Sahure (Sephres) → Neferirkare Kakai → Shepseskare → Neferefre → Nyuserre Ini → Menkauhor → Djedkare Isesi → Unas (Onnus, Pyramid Texts!)
nodes.role: Sun Temple Builders & Oldest Religious Texts (Pyramid Texts of Unas)
nodes.notes: Userkaf's era compiled the Palermo Stone Annals; Unas inscribed the oldest corpus of sacred funerary liturgy in human history (Pyramid Texts) inside his Saqqara pyramid.

nodes.name: Dynasty VI Complete (6-7 Kings): Teti (Othoes) → Userkare → Pepi I (Phius) → Merenre I → Pepi II (Phiops, 94-yr reign!) → Merenre II → Queen Nitocris (Neith-iqerty)
nodes.role: Longest Reign in History (Pepi II) & End of the Old Kingdom
nodes.notes: Pepi II ascended at age 6 and ruled into his 90s (Manetho: 94 yrs!). Manetho & Herodotus name Queen Nitocris ('bravest and most beautiful woman of her time') closing the Old Kingdom.

nodes.name: First Intermediate Period (Dynasties VII–X): Memphite Ephemerals (Neferkare Pepyseneb) & Heracleopolitan Kings (Khety / Achthoes I–III, Merikare)
nodes.era: c. 2168-2040 BCE (Manetho Fr. 23-30; Breasted Vol. I)
nodes.role: Fragmented Rival Houses of Memphis & Heracleopolis
nodes.notes: Manetho's famous '70 kings in 70 days' (Dyn. VII) and Khety/Achthoes of Heracleopolis (Dyn. IX-X, author of 'Teaching for King Merikare').

nodes.name: Dynasty XI Complete (Theban Reunifiers): Intef I → Intef II → Mentuhotep I → Intef III → Mentuhotep II (Reunified Egypt!) → Mentuhotep III → Mentuhotep IV
nodes.era: c. 2160-2000 BCE (Breasted Vol. I §63; Manetho Fr. 31-32)
nodes.role: Theban Unifiers of the Middle Kingdom
nodes.notes: Mentuhotep II defeated Heracleopolis, reunited Upper & Lower Egypt, and built the terraced mortuary temple at Deir el-Bahari.

nodes.name: Dynasty XII Complete (Golden Age of Middle Kingdom): Amenemhat I → Senusret I (Sesonchosis) → Amenemhat II → Senusret II → Senusret III (Sesostris) → Amenemhat III (Lamares, Labyrinth!) → Amenemhat IV → Queen Sobekneferu (Scemiophris)
nodes.role: Classical Peak of Egyptian Literature, Faiyum Irrigation & Nubian Fortresses
nodes.notes: Manetho preserves direct parent-child links: Amenemhat I -> son Senusret I -> Amenemhat II -> Senusret II -> Senusret III -> son Amenemhat III (built the Great Labyrinth at Hawara) -> Amenemhat IV -> sister Queen Sobekneferu (first fully attested female Pharaoh!).

nodes.name: Dynasties XIII (60 Theban Kings: Sobekhotep IV / Chenephres, Dedumose / Tutimaeus) & XIV (76 Xoite Kings of the Eastern Delta)
nodes.role: Second Intermediate Period Fragmentation & Asiatic Delta Settlers
nodes.notes: Waddell notes Sobekhotep IV = Chenephres (in Artapanus's Moses account!) and Dedumose = Tutimaeus ('in whose reign a blast of God smote us' and the Hyksos entered Egypt!).

nodes.name: Dynasties XV–XVII: Great Hyksos Kings (Salitis, Bnon, Apachnan, Khyan/Iannas, Apophis/Apepi, Khamudi/Assis) vs. Theban Liberators (Seqenenre Tao & Kamose)
nodes.era: c. 1650-1550 BCE (Manetho Fr. 42-49 via Josephus Against Apion)
nodes.role: Semitic Shepherd Kings of Avaris & War of Liberation
nodes.notes: Josephus (quoting Manetho verbatim!) preserved the 6 Great Hyksos rulers of Avaris (Salitis, Bnon, Apachnan, Apophis [traditional Pharaoh of Joseph in Syncellus!], Khyan, Assis) until Theban Seqenenre Tao & son Kamose launched the liberation finished by Ahmose I.

nodes.name: Dynasty XVIII Early–Mid: Ahmose I → Amenhotep I → Thutmose I → Thutmose II & Queen Hatshepsut (Amessis) → Thutmose III → Amenhotep II → Thutmose IV
nodes.role: Imperial Expansion to the Euphrates & Sole Female Pharaoh Hatshepsut
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Hatshepsut (Manetho's Amessis) sent the famous trade expedition to Punt; Thutmose III (Battle of Megiddo) expanded Egypt to its greatest extent; Thutmose IV erected the Dream Stele between the Sphinx's paws.

nodes.name: Dynasty XVIII Late (Amarna & Post-Amarna): Amenhotep III (+ Queen Tiye) → Akhenaten (+ Nefertiti) → Smenkhkare → Tutankhamun → Ay → Horemheb (Harmais = Danaus!)
nodes.role: Monotheistic Amarna Revolution & Greco-Egyptian Danaus/Aegyptus Bridge
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho explicitly equates General/Pharaoh Horemheb ('Harmais') with Greek Danaus and Ramesses/Seti with his brother Aegyptus — linking Greek Argive genealogy directly into Egypt's 18th/19th Dynasty transition!

nodes.name: Dynasty XIX Complete: Ramesses I → Seti I (Sethos) → Ramesses II (Rapsaces, 67 yrs) → Merneptah (Israel Stele) → Amenmesse → Seti II & Siptah → Queen Twosret (Thuoris — Fall of Troy!)
nodes.role: Ramesside Empire & Manetho's Synchronism with the Trojan War
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Manetho notes under Queen Twosret ('Thuoris', identified with Homer's Polybus & Alcandra) Troy was taken — synchronizing Egypt's 19th Dynasty directly with the Bronze Age Collapse & Trojan War!

nodes.name: Dynasty XX Complete (10 Ramessides): Setnakhte → Ramesses III (Medinet Habu, Sea Peoples!) → Ramesses IV → V → VI → VII → VIII → IX → X → Ramesses XI
nodes.era: 1189-1077 BCE (Budge Book of Kings Vol. II pp. 1-20; Manetho Fr. 57)
nodes.role: Defense Against the Sea Peoples & End of the New Kingdom
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Budge Vol. II lists all 10 sons of Ramesses III from Medinet Habu (incl. Ramesses IV, VI, VIII) and the complete Ramesside succession down to Ramesses XI, when High Priest Herihor seized Upper Egypt.

nodes.name: Dynasty XXI (Divided Egypt): Tanite Kings (Smendes, Psusennes I [Silver Pharaoh!], Amenemope, Osochor, Siamun, Psusennes II) & Theban Priest-Kings (Herihor → Piankh → Pinudjem I → Menkheperre → Pinudjem II)
nodes.era: 1077-943 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 20-34; Manetho Fr. 58-59)
nodes.role: Biblical Era of David & Solomon (Siamun & Psusennes II)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Psusennes I's intact silver sarcophagus was found at Tanis; Siamun campaigned in Philistia/Gezer (often identified as the Pharaoh whose daughter married King Solomon, 1 Kgs 3:1, 9:16!); Psusennes II's daughters Karamat & Maatkare married into the Libyan 22nd Dynasty!

nodes.name: Dynasty XXII Complete (Libyan/Bubastite — Stele of Pasenhor): Buiu-uaua → Shoshenq I (Shishak!) → Osorkon I → Takelot I → Osorkon II → Shoshenq II → Takelot II → Shoshenq III → Pami → Shoshenq V
nodes.era: 943-716 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 35-60; Manetho Fr. 60-61)
nodes.role: Complete 15-Generation Meshwesh Libyan Genealogy & Shishak's Sack of Jerusalem
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: The famous Serapeum Stele of Pasenhor (Budge pp. 35-39) traces Shoshenq I back 6 generations to Libyan chief Buyuwawa and forward through Osorkon II! Shoshenq I (= Biblical Shishak, 1 Kgs 14:25) invaded Rehoboam's Judah in 925 BCE.

nodes.name: Dynasties XXIII (Pedubast I, Osorkon III, Takelot III, Rudamun) & XXIV (Tefnakht I → Bakenranef / Bocchoris)
nodes.era: 818-715 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 60-69; Manetho Fr. 62-65)
nodes.role: Libyan Delta Coalitions Resisting Kushite Reunification
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Tefnakht of Sais led the Delta coalition against Kushite King Piye (Piankhi Stele); his son Bakenranef (Greek: Bocchoris, famous lawgiver) was defeated by Kushite Shabaka.

nodes.name: Dynasty XXV Complete (Kushite Pharaohs): Kashta (+ Pebatjma) → Piye & Shabaka (Sabacon) → Shabataka (Sebichos) → Taharqa (Tirhakah) → Tantamani (Ammeris)
nodes.era: 744-656 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 70-78, 195-199; Manetho Fr. 66-67)
nodes.role: Nubian Reunifiers of Egypt & Biblical Allies of Hezekiah
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Budge details the entire royal family including God's Wives of Amun Amenirdis I & Shepenupet II, linking Kushite bloodlines into Dynasty XXVI!

nodes.name: Dynasty XXVI Complete (Saite Renaissance): Necho I → Psamtik I (54 yrs) → Necho II (Battle of Megiddo/Carchemish!) → Psamtik II → Apries (Biblical Hophra!) → Amasis II (44 yrs) → Psamtik III
nodes.era: 664-525 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 78-90; Manetho Fr. 68-69; Jer 44:30)
nodes.role: Last Great Native Renaissance Before Persian Conquest
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Necho II slew King Josiah at Megiddo (609 BCE); Apries (Biblical Pharaoh Hophra, Jer 44:30) sheltered Judean refugees including Jeremiah; Amasis II allied with Croesus of Lydia & Polycrates of Samos; Psamtik III fell to Cambyses II (525 BCE).

nodes.name: Dynasties XXVII–XXXI: 1st Persian (Cambyses, Darius I, Xerxes, Artaxerxes I), XXVIII (Amyrtaeus), XXIX (Nepherites I, Hakor/Achoris), XXX (Nectanebo I, Teos, Nectanebo II — Last Native Pharaoh!) & XXXI (Artaxerxes III, Arses, Darius III)
nodes.era: 525-332 BCE (Budge Vol. II pp. 91-106; Manetho Fr. 70-75)
nodes.role: Final Native Egyptian Resistance Through Nectanebo II to Alexander (332 BCE)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Amyrtaeus freed Egypt from Persia (404 BCE); Nectanebo I & II (Dynasty XXX, builders of Philae & Karnak pylons) were the LAST native Egyptian Pharaohs in history before Alexander the Great entered Egypt in 332 BCE!

nodes.name: Complete Ptolemaic Dynasty (All 15 Ptolemies & 7 Cleopatras): Ptolemy I Soter → II Philadelphus (Septuagint!) → III Euergetes → IV Philopator → V Epiphanes (Rosetta Stone! + Cleopatra I Syra) → VI Philometor → VIII Euergetes II → IX Soter II → XII Auletes → Cleopatra VII & Caesarion
nodes.role: Macedonian-Greek Pharaohs of Alexandria (Septuagint & Rosetta Stone)
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II
nodes.notes: Ptolemy II built the Library of Alexandria & commissioned the Greek Septuagint; Ptolemy V (+ Seleucid Cleopatra I Syra) issued the Rosetta Stone (196 BCE); Cleopatra VII & Caesarion (Ptolemy XV) closed 3,000 years of Pharaonic rule.

nodes.name: Napatan Kings of Kush: Atlanersa → Senkamanisken → Anlamani → Aspelta → Harsiotef → Nastasen
nodes.role: Post-25th Dynasty Nubian Pyramid Builders of Nuri & Jebel Barkal
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp. 199-205)
nodes.notes: After Assyria pushed Dynasty XXV south of Aswan, Taharqa & Tantamani's successors (Atlanersa, Senkamanisken, Aspelta [moved capital to Meroe after Psamtik II's 593 BCE raid], Harsiotef, Nastasen) ruled Kush for centuries.

nodes.name: Meroitic Kingdom: King Arqamani (Ergamenes) → King Natakamani & Queen Amanitore → Princes Arikhankharer & Shorkaror
nodes.era: c. 270 BCE – 50 CE (Budge Vol. II pp. 205-214; Diodorus III.6; Acts 8:27)
nodes.role: Golden Age of Meroe, Meroitic Script & Biblical Candace Dynasty
sources: Budge Book of the Kings of Egypt Vol. II (pp. 205-214)
nodes.notes: Arqamani (Greek: Ergamenes, friend of Ptolemy II & IV!) broke priestly control and built Dakka temple; King Natakamani & Kandake Queen Amanitore (Biblical 'Candace' era!) built the Lion Temple at Naqa and restored Meroe.

nodes.name: Targamos (Togarmah) → 8 Caucasian Hero-Sons: Haos (Armenia), Kartlos (Georgia), Bardos, Movak'an, Lek' (Dagestan), Heros, K'avk'as (North Caucasus) & Egros (Colchis)
nodes.era: Caucasian Table of Nations (Kartlis Tskhovreba pp. 13-18)
nodes.role: Patriarchal Origin of All Peoples of the Caucasus
nodes.notes: Targamos (Togarmah, lived 600 yrs between Mt. Ararat & Masis) divided the Caucasus among 8 sons: eldest Haos (slew Nimrod/Nebroth with an arrow! Progenitor of Armenians), Kartlos (Georgians), Bardos (Barda), Movak'an (Albania), Lek' (Lezgins), Heros (Hereti), K'avk'as (Durdzuks/Vainakhs), Egros (Megrels/Colchis) — plus Khazar prince Uobos (Ossetians)!

nodes.name: Kartlos's 5 Sons (Mtskhetos, Gardabos, K'akhos, K'ukhos, Gachios) → Mtskhetos's 3 Sons (Uplos, Odzrkhos, Javakhos)
nodes.role: Founders of Mtskheta, Kakheti, Gardabani, Uplistsikhe & Javakheti
nodes.notes: Kartlos's widow divided Kartli among his 5 sons; preeminent Mtskhetos founded Mtskheta and fathered Uplos (Uplistsikhe — ancestor of King Parnavaz I!), Odzrkhos, and Javakhos.

nodes.name: Kings of Iberia/Kartli (1–23): Pharnavazids (Parnavaz I → Saurmag), Nebrotids (Mirvan I, Parnajom, Mirvan II) & Arshak'ids (Arshak I, Aderk'i, Parsman the Valiant, Rev I → Aspagur)
nodes.role: First Royal Dynasties of Georgia & Creator of the Georgian Script (Parnavaz I)
nodes.notes: Parnavaz I (kinsman of Uplos, mother from Isfahan, allied with Kuji of Egrisi) defeated Alexander's governor Azon and created the Georgian alphabet! Followed by Nimrodid ('Nebrotid') and Armenian-Parthian Arshak'id lines down to last Pharnavazid Aspagur -> daughter Abeshuru.

nodes.name: Chosroid (Mihranid-Sasanian) Dynasty (24–33+): King Mirian III (+ St. Nino, Christianized Georgia 337 CE!) → Bakar → Archil → King Vakht'ang I Gorgasali (Founder of Tbilisi!) → Dachi
nodes.role: Christianizers of Georgia & Founder of Tbilisi (Sasanian-Iberian Bloodline)
nodes.notes: Mirian III (Persian prince Mikhran, son of a Sasanian king; married Pharnavazid heiress Abeshuru & Queen Nana) embraced Christianity via St. Nino of Cappadocia! Descendant King Vakht'ang Gorgasali ('Wolf-Head', married both a Persian princess Balendukht & Byzantine princess Helen!) founded Tbilisi!

nodes.name: Bagrat'ioni Dynasty (Sumbat Davitisdze): King David → Joseph's Brother K'leop'a (26 Gens!) → 7 Brothers (Bagrat' & Guaram Kuropalates) → Ashot' the Great → Bagrat' III (1st King of Unified Georgia, 1008!) → David IV the Builder & Queen Tamar
nodes.role: World's Longest-Reigning Christian Royal House (Claiming Direct Davidic Descent via Clopas!)
nodes.notes: Uniquely bridges Matthew 1 -> Joseph's brother K'leop'a -> 26 generations -> 7 brothers baptized by Queen Rakael -> Bagrat' & Guaram Kuropalates -> Ashot' I the Great (d. 826) -> Bagrat' III (united Abkhazia & Kartli, d. 1014) -> Giorgi I -> David IV the Builder -> Queen Tamar the Great!

nodes.name: Parthian / Ashkanian Empire (Arsacids): Ashk ben Ashkan (Al-Biruni Traces to Kayanian Siyavush!) → Arsaces I → Mithridates I & II → Phraates → Orodes II → Vologases → Artabanus IV
nodes.era: 247 BCE – 224 CE (Al-Biruni pp. 116-120; Betham Tab. CV)
nodes.role: 470-Year Iranian Superpower Rivaling Rome (Bridged to Kayanian Siyavush!)
nodes.notes: Al-Biruni (p. 116) gives the Persian royal pedigree of Ashk ben Ashkan (Arsaces) directly back to Kayanian Prince Siyawush ben Kay Kavus — uniting historical Parthia with the Avestan/Shahnameh Kayanians! Defeated Crassus at Carrhae (53 BCE) and placed Tiridates on Armenia's throne.

nodes.name: Sasanian Empire (Al-Biruni Pedigree from Kay Bahman & Esfandiyar!): Sasan → Papak → Ardashir I → Shapur I → Shapur II → Bahram V Gur → Kavadh I → Khosrow I Anushirvan → Khosrow II Parviz → Queen Boran → Yazdegerd III
nodes.role: Last Pre-Islamic Persian Empire & Ancestor of Buwayhids, Bavandids & Samanids
nodes.notes: Al-Biruni (p. 122) traces Ardashir I -> Babak -> Sasan -> Bahman -> Isfandiyar! Also preserves complete medieval pedigrees of the Buwayhids (14 gens from Bahram Gur, p. 45), Bavandids/Ziyarids (11 gens from Kavadh I, p. 47), and Samanids (9 gens from Bahram Chobin, p. 48)!

nodes.name: Afrighid Shahs of Khwarazm (Complete 22-Gen Line in Al-Biruni!): Siyawush → Kay Khosrow → Afrigh (305 CE) → Baghra → Arthamukh → Askajamuk → Shawushfar → Abu 'Abdallah Muhammad (d. 995 CE)
nodes.role: Al-Biruni's Own Homeland Dynasty — 22 Unbroken Generations from Kayanian Siyawush!
nodes.notes: Preserved intact by Al-Biruni (himself a native of Khwarazm!): 22 unbroken father-to-son Khwarazmshahs starting with Afrigh's castle behind Alfir (305 CE) down to the last Afrighid martyr Abu 'Abdallah Muhammad (995 CE)!

nodes.name: Pre-Islamic Arab Kingdoms: Himyarite Tubbas of Yemen (Bilkis, Castle Ghumdan, Dhu-Nuwas, Dhu-Yazan), Lakhmids of Al-Hirah (Imru' al-Qays → Al-Mundhir → Al-Nu'man III) & Ghassanids (Al-Harith)
nodes.era: c. 110 BCE – 636 CE (Al-Biruni pp. 40-50, 311, 384; Kebra Nagast Ch. 117)
nodes.role: Qahtanite / South Arabian & Syro-Mesopotamian Pre-Islamic Arab Monarchies
nodes.notes: Himyarite Tubba kings of Yemen (Castle Ghumdan in San'a, Dhu-al-Manar, Dhu-Nuwas [clashed with King Kaleb of Aksum over Najran in 525 CE!], Saif ibn Dhi-Yazan), Persian-allied Lakhmid kings of Al-Hirah (Battle of Dhu Qar!), and Byzantine-allied Christian Ghassanid kings of Syria!

nodes.name: Kebra Nagast Royal Court: Pre-Makeda Kings (Arawi → Angabo → Gedur → Sebado → Kawnasya), Merchant Tamrin & High Priest 'Azaryas (Son of Zadok) + 21 Israelite Firstborn Nobles
nodes.era: c. 960 BCE (Kebra Nagast Ch. 22-48, Intro p. xxxv)
nodes.role: Bearers of the Ark of the Covenant (Zion) from Jerusalem to Aksum
sources: Kebra Nagast (Budge 1922 Intro p. xxxv, Ch. 22-48, p. 62)
nodes.notes: Budge's Oxford MS lists 5 pre-Makeda kings (Arawi -> Angabo -> Gedur -> Sebado -> Kawnasya -> Queen Makeda). Merchant Tamrin linked Ethiopia to Solomon; 'Azaryas (son of High Priest Zadok) and 20 named firstborn sons of Israelite nobles carried the Ark of the Covenant with Menyelek I (Bayna-Lehkem / David II) to Aksum!

nodes.name: Kebra Nagast World-Kingdoms Bridge: 'Adrami (Youngest Son of Solomon → King of Rome via 'Adlonya!), Fares → Persia & 'Akamhel (Son of Samson & Delilah → Philistia)
nodes.role: Ethiopic Universal Theology Tracing Rome, Ethiopia, Persia & Philistia to Israel!
nodes.notes: Remarkable medieval cross-cultural genealogical synthesis: Solomon's youngest son 'Adrami marries 'Adlonya (daughter of Roman king Baltasar) to become King of Rome/Byzantium! Also traces Fars (Persia) to Judah's son Perez (Fares) and Philistia's kings to Samson & Delilah's posthumous son 'Akamhel (Menahem)!

nodes.name: Aksumite & Solomonic Restoration: King Kaleb of Aksum (Allied with Emperor Justinus!) → Israel & Gabra Maskal → Zagwe Lalibala → Emperor Yekuno 'Amlak (1270 CE)
nodes.era: c. 520-1285 CE (Kebra Nagast Ch. 117 & Colophon, Budge pp. 225-229)
nodes.role: 6th-Century Aksumite Expedition to Yemen & 1270 CE Solomonic Restoration
nodes.notes: King Kaleb of Aksum met Byzantine Emperor Justinus I in Jerusalem to divide the Christian world and defeated Himyarite King Dhu-Nuwas in Yemen (525 CE), abdicating to his son Gabra Maskal. After the Zagwe interlude (Takla Haymanot -> Lalibala), Yekuno 'Amlak restored the Solomonic Dynasty in 1270 CE!

nodes.name: Hesiodic Primordials: Chaos → Nyx/Erebus & Gaia → Pontus (Phorcys, Ceto, Gorgons, Nereus & 50 Nereids incl. Thetis)
nodes.role: Sea Deities, Gorgons & Ancestors of Achilles's Mother Thetis
nodes.notes: Pontus + Gaia -> Phorcys & Ceto (Graiae, Gorgons Stheno/Euryale/Medusa -> Pegasus & Chrysaor -> Geryon & Echidna!) and Nereus + Doris -> 50 Nereids (Amphitrite, Thetis [mother of Achilles!], Calypso, Galatea).

nodes.name: Complete 12 Titans: Oceanus/Tethys, Coeus/Phoebe (Leto/Asteria), Hyperion/Theia (Helios/Selene/Eos), Crius (Astraeus/Pallas/Perses → Hecate), Iapetus & Cronus/Rhea
nodes.notes: Hyperion + Theia -> Helios (father of Circe, Pasiphae & Aeetes of Colchis -> Medea!), Selene, Eos (mother of Memnon & Phaethon). Coeus + Phoebe -> Leto (mother of Apollo & Artemis) & Asteria (mother of Hecate). Pallas + Styx -> Nike, Cratos, Zelus, Bia.

nodes.name: Zeus & Mnemosyne → 9 Muses (Calliope → Orpheus & Linus), Horae, Moerae (Fates) & Charites (Graces)
nodes.role: Divine Patrons of Arts, Fate & Mythic Poets
nodes.notes: Calliope + Oeagrus (or Apollo) -> Orpheus (Argonaut & singer) & Linus; Zeus + Themis -> 3 Horae (Eirene, Eunomia, Dike) & 3 Fates (Clotho, Lachesis, Atropos); Zeus + Demeter -> Persephone; Zeus + Metis -> Athena.

nodes.name: Aethlius & Calyce → Endymion → Aetolus → Porthaon → Oeneus → Meleager, Deianira & Tydeus → Diomedes
nodes.role: Aetolian Royal House (Calydonian Boar Hunt & Hero Diomedes of Troy)
nodes.notes: Calyce (daughter of Aeolus) + Aethlius (son of Protogonia dau. of Deucalion) -> Endymion -> Aetolus -> Pleuron/Calydon -> Agenor -> Porthaon -> Oeneus (+ Althaea -> Meleager & Deianira [wife of Heracles!]; + Periboea -> Tydeus [Seven Against Thebes] -> Diomedes [Iliad hero!]).

nodes.name: Salmoneus → Tyro (+ Poseidon) → Pelias (Iolcus) & Neleus (Pylos) → Nestor (Trojan War Counselor)
nodes.role: Neleid Kings of Pylos & Pelias of Iolcus
nodes.notes: Tyro bore twins Pelias (usurped Iolcus -> Alcestis & Acastus) and Neleus (+ Chloris -> 12 sons, of whom only Nestor survived Heracles's raid, becoming the wise elder king of Pylos at Troy -> Antilochus & Pisistratus!).

nodes.name: Cretheus → Aeson → Jason (Argonauts + Medea of Colchis), Amythaon (Melampus/Adrastus) & Pheres (Admetus)
nodes.role: Cretheid House of Iolcus, Seer Melampus & Leader of the Argonauts
nodes.notes: Aeson -> Jason (led the Argonauts to Colchis to win the Golden Fleece from King Aeetes; married Medea -> Medeus/Medus, eponymous ancestor of the Medes in Greek myth!). Amythaon -> Melampus (seer -> Amphiaraus) & Bias -> Talaus -> King Adrastus of Argos.

nodes.name: Sisyphus (+ Merope) → Glaucus → Bellerophon (Slayer of the Chimera) & Phrixus/Helle (Athamas)
nodes.role: Corinthian & Boeotian Aeolids (Pegasus, Chimera & Golden Fleece)
nodes.notes: Sisyphus (founder of Corinth) -> Glaucus -> Bellerophon (rode winged Pegasus to slay the Chimera in Lycia -> grandfather of Trojan War allies Glaucus & Sarpedon!). Athamas -> Phrixus & Helle (origin of the Golden Fleece & Hellespont!).

nodes.name: Hypermnestra & Lynceus → Abas → Acrisius (→ Danaë → Perseus) & Proetus (Tiryns)
nodes.role: Sole Surviving Danaid Line Bridging Egypt (Belus/Aegyptus) to Perseus
nodes.notes: Hypermnestra spared her husband Lynceus (son of Aegyptus), becoming ancestor of all later Argive & Mycenaean kings: Abas -> twin kings Acrisius (Argos -> Danae + Zeus -> Perseus!) and Proetus (Tiryns -> Megapenthes).

nodes.name: Perseus & Andromeda → Perses, Alcaeus (→ Amphitryon), Sthenelus (→ Eurystheus) & Electryon (→ Alcmene → Heracles)
nodes.role: Complete Perseid Royal House of Mycenae & Tiryns
nodes.notes: Perseus's sons married daughters of Pelops: Sthenelus -> Eurystheus (taskmaster of Heracles's 12 Labors); Alcaeus -> Amphitryon; Electryon -> Alcmene (bore Heracles by Zeus & twin Iphicles -> Iolaus by Amphitryon!).

nodes.name: Return of the Heraclidae: Heracles → Hyllus → Cleodaeus → Aristomachus → Temenus (Argos), Cresphontes (Messene) & Aristodemus (→ Eurysthenes & Procles of Sparta!)
nodes.role: Dorian Conquest of the Peloponnese & Dual Kingship of Sparta
nodes.notes: Three generations after Hyllus, the Heraclidae conquered the Peloponnese with the Dorians: Temenus received Argos (ancestors of the Argead Kings of Macedon -> Alexander the Great!); Cresphontes took Messene; Aristodemus's twins Eurysthenes & Procles founded the Agiad & Eurypontid dual royal dynasties of Sparta (down to Leonidas of Thermopylae!).

nodes.name: Minos & Pasiphaë → Catreus (→ Aerope), Deucalion (→ Idomeneus), Ariadne, Phaedra & Minotaur
nodes.role: Complete Cretan Royal Family (Bridging Minos to Agamemnon & Theseus!)
nodes.notes: Minos's son Catreus fathered Aerope (mother of Agamemnon & Menelaus!) and Clymene (mother of Palamedes); son Deucalion fathered Trojan War commander Idomeneus; daughters Ariadne & Phaedra linked Crete to Theseus of Athens.

nodes.name: Cadmus & Harmonia → Polydorus → Labdacus → Laius (+ Jocasta) → Oedipus → Eteocles, Polynices, Antigone & Ismene (Seven Against Thebes & Epigoni)
nodes.role: Complete Labdacid Dynasty of Thebes (Plus Semele → Dionysus & Illyrius)
nodes.notes: Cadmus's daughters: Semele (mother of Dionysus), Ino, Autonoe (mother of Actaeon), Agave (mother of Pentheus). Son Illyrius (eponym of Illyria!). Polydorus -> Labdacus -> Laius -> Oedipus -> Seven Against Thebes (Polynices, Adrastus, Tydeus, Amphiaraus, Capaneus, Hippomedon, Parthenopaeus) & Epigoni (Alcmaeon, Diomedes, Thersander).

nodes.name: Pelasgus → Lycaon (50 Sons & Callisto) → Arcas → Aleus (→ Auge + Heracles → Telephus) & Atalanta
nodes.role: Autochthonous Pelasgian Kings of Arcadia & Heroine Atalanta
nodes.notes: Lycaon's impiety triggered Deucalion's Flood (only son Nyctimus survived); Callisto + Zeus -> Arcas (eponym of Arcadia & Ursa Major) -> Elatus & Aphidas -> Aleus -> Auge (+ Heracles -> King Telephus of Mysia!) & Lycurgus -> Iasus -> Atalanta (mother of Parthenopaeus).

nodes.name: Atlas & Pleione → 7 Pleiades (Maia → Hermes; Taygete → Lacedaemon → Tyndareus + Leda → Helen, Clytemnestra, Castor & Pollux; Icarius → Penelope)
nodes.role: Complete Atlantid Line of Hermes, Sparta, Helen of Troy & Penelope
nodes.notes: Lacedaemon (+ Sparta) -> Amyclas -> Cynortes -> Perieres/Oebalus -> Tyndareus (+ Leda -> Helen, Clytemnestra, Dioscuri Castor & Pollux) & Icarius (father of Penelope, wife of Odysseus!). Leucippus's daughter Arsinoe/Coronis + Apollo -> Asclepius (god of medicine!).

nodes.name: Asopus → Aegina (+ Zeus) → Aeacus → Telamon (→ Ajax & Teucer) & Peleus (+ Thetis → Achilles → Neoptolemus)
nodes.role: Aeacid Heroes of the Trojan War & Ancestors of Olympias/Alexander!
nodes.notes: Aeacus (Judge of the Dead) fathered Telamon (King of Salamis -> Ajax the Great & Teucer [founder of Salamis in Cyprus!]) and Peleus (+ Nereid Thetis -> Achilles -> Neoptolemus/Pyrrhus, ancestor of the Molossian Kings of Epirus, Queen Olympias [mother of Alexander the Great!], and King Pyrrhus!).

nodes.name: Kings of Athens: Cecrops → Erichthonius → Pandion I (Procne/Philomela) → Erechtheus (Creusa/Orithyia) → Aegeus → Theseus → Demophon
nodes.era: Attic Heroic Era (Apollodorus III.xiv.1-Epit. I; Eusebius)
nodes.role: Complete Mythic Royal Genealogy of Athens (Slayer of the Minotaur)
nodes.notes: Earth-born Cecrops (1st King of Athens) -> Erichthonius -> Pandion I -> Erechtheus (daughter Creusa married Xuthus -> Ion, eponym of Ionians!) -> Pandion II -> Aegeus (+ Aethra of Troezen, dau. of Pittheus son of Pelops!) -> Theseus (slew Minotaur; + Antiope -> Hippolytus; + Phaedra -> Acamas & Demophon).

nodes.name: Tantalus → Niobe & Pelops (+ Hippodamia) → Atreus, Thyestes & Pittheus → Agamemnon, Menelaus, Aegisthus, Iphigenia, Electra & Orestes
nodes.role: Complete House of Atreus from Tantalus to Orestes & Tisamenus
nodes.notes: Tantalus -> Pelops (eponym of Peloponnese!) -> Atreus (+ Aerope of Crete -> Agamemnon & Menelaus), Thyestes (-> Aegisthus), Pittheus (grandfather of Theseus!), plus daughters Astydamia/Nicippe/Lysidice (mothers of Perseids!). Agamemnon + Clytemnestra -> Orestes (+ Hermione -> Tisamenus, slain by Heraclidae!), Electra & Iphigenia.

nodes.name: Ayodhya Solar Spine (Gens 2–30): Ikshvaku → Vikukshi → Kakutstha → Yuvanashva I → Shravasta → Kuvalashva → Yuvanashva II → Mandhatri → Purukutsa → Trasadasyu → Trayyaruna
nodes.era: Satya Yuga (Pargiter Master Table Gens 2-30, p. 145)
nodes.role: First 30 Generations of the Solar Dynasty of Ayodhya
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 90-92, 145
nodes.notes: Complete early Aikshvaku kings: Shravasta founded Shravasti; Emperor Mandhatri (Gen 21) conquered the Pauravas & Druhyus; son Purukutsa married Narmada; grandson Trasadasyu is celebrated in the Rigveda!

nodes.name: Ayodhya Solar Spine (Gens 31–64): Trishanku → Harishchandra → Rohita → Bahu → Sagara → Asamanjas → Amshumant → Bhagiratha → Ambarisha → Rituparna → Kalmashapada → Dilipa II → Raghu → Aja → Dasharatha
nodes.era: Treta Yuga (Pargiter Master Table Gens 31-64, pp. 145, 147)
nodes.role: Golden Era of the Solar Dynasty Leading to Lord Rama
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 92-94, 145-147
nodes.notes: Satyavrata-Trishanku & truthful King Harishchandra (Gen 32); Emperor Sagara (Gen 41, destroyed the Haihaya raiders!); Bhagiratha (Gen 45, brought the Ganges to earth); Rituparna (Gen 51, host of Nala!); Dilipa II -> Raghu -> Aja -> Dasharatha (Gen 64).

nodes.name: Ayodhya Post-Rama Spine (Gens 66–95): Kusha → Atithi → Nishadha → Nala → Hiranyanabha (Yoga Master!) → Pushya → Agnivarna → Maru → Brihadbala (Slain at Kurukshetra) → Brihatkshaya
nodes.era: Dvapara Yuga (Pargiter Master Table Gens 66-95, p. 149)
nodes.role: 30 Generations from Rama's Son Kusha to the Mahabharata War
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 94-95, 149
nodes.notes: Complete post-Rama Solar kings down to Gen 94 King Brihadbala of Kosala (slain by Arjuna's son Abhimanyu at the Bharata Battle, c. 950 BCE!) and continuing via Divakara to the Shakya clan of Gautama Buddha!

nodes.name: Videha / Mithila Solar Dynasty (All 54 Kings): Nimi → Mithi Janaka → Udavasu → Hrasvaroman → Siradhvaja Janaka (Father of Sita!) & Kushadhvaja → Bahulashva → Kritakshana → Janaka-Ugrasena
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 95-96, 145-149
nodes.notes: Founded by Ikshvaku's son Nimi -> Mithi Janaka (founder of Mithila). Siradhvaja Janaka (Gen 64, contemporary of Dasharatha) discovered Goddess Sita; post-battle Janaka-Ugrasena & Janaka-Dharmadhvaja appear in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad with sage Yajnavalkya!

nodes.name: Manu's Other Solar Kingdoms: Vaisali (Nabhanedishtha → Bhalandana → Marutta → Trinabindu → Vishala → Pramati), Sharyatas (Anarta/Dvaraka → Raivata Kakudmin) & Nabhagas (Ambarisha → Rathitara)
nodes.role: Ancient Dynasties of North Bihar (Vaisali) & Gujarat (Anarta)
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 97-98, 145-147
nodes.notes: Nabhanedishtha's line produced Emperor Marutta (Gen 40), Trinabindu (whose daughter Ilavila married Rishi Pulastya -> Vishravas -> Kubera & Ravana!), and Vishala (founder of Vaisali). Sharyati's line ruled Anarta (Gujarat), whose princess Revati married Balarama!

nodes.name: Kanyakubja Dynasty (Amavasu Line): Amavasu → Bhima → Jahnu → Kusha → Kushika → King Gadhi → Vishvamitra (Kshatriya-Turned-Brahmarshi!) → Ashtaka → Lauhi
nodes.role: Aila Kingdom of Kanauj & Origin of the Gayatri Mantra Rishi Vishvamitra
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 99-101, 234-237
nodes.notes: Pururavas's second son Amavasu founded Kanyakubja -> Jahnu (adopted River Ganga as 'Jahnavi') -> Gadhi (whose daughter Satyavati married Bhargava Richika -> Jamadagni -> Parashurama!) -> Vishvaratha-Vishvamitra (composer of Rigveda Mandala III & Gayatri Mantra; adopted Shunahshepa-Devarata!).

nodes.name: Kasi (Varanasi) Dynasty: Kshatravriddha → Sunahotra → Kasha → Dhanvantari (Father of Ayurveda!) → Divodasa I & II → Pratardana → Alarka → Subahu
nodes.era: Gens 5-94 (Pargiter Ch. IX p. 101; Ch. XIII pp. 153-155)
nodes.role: Ancient Sacred Kingdom of Varanasi & Origin of Ayurveda
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 101, 145-155
nodes.notes: Ayu's son Kshatravriddha founded Kasi (Varanasi); King Dhanvantari is revered as the founder of Ayurvedic medicine; Divodasa II & Pratardana (Gen 41) broke Haihaya dominance alongside Sagara of Ayodhya!

nodes.name: Haihaya Dynasty (Yadu → Sahasrajit): Haihaya → Mahishmant (Mahishmati) → Bhadrashrenya → Kritavirya → Emperor Kartavirya Arjuna → Jayadhvaja → Talajanghas (5 Clans)
nodes.role: Central Indian Narmada Empire & Nemesis of Parashurama & Sagara
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 102, 144-146, 153-156
nodes.notes: Kartavirya Arjuna (Gen 31, thousand-armed emperor of Mahishmati) captured Ravana, raided Kasi and Ayodhya, and clashed fatally with Bhargava Parashurama; his descendants the 5 Talajangha clans (Vitihotras, Bhojas, Avantis, Sharyatas, Tundikeras) were finally crushed by Sagara (Gen 41).

nodes.name: Yadava Main Line (Kroshtu → Satvata): Shashabindu → Jyamagha → Vidarbha (Cedi & Kratha-Bhima) → Madhu → Satvata → Andhaka (Kukura → Ugrasena → Kamsa) & Vrishni (Shura → Vasudeva → Krishna → Samba & Vajra)
nodes.role: Complete Yadava Pedigree from Yadu to Krishna, Kamsa & Surviving Heir Vajra
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 102-107, 144-148, 284
nodes.notes: Unites ALL Yadava branches: Shashabindu (Gen 20), Jyamagha -> Vidarbha (founder of Vidarbha & Cedi), Madhu (eponym of Mathura/Madhava), Satvata -> Andhaka (Ugrasena -> King Kamsa; Kritavarman) & Vrishni (Devamidhusha -> Shura -> Vasudeva & Kunti -> Krishna, Balarama, Satyaki; grandson Vajra installed at Indraprastha!).

nodes.name: Druhyus (Gandhara → Pracetas — Northward Migration Beyond India!) & Turvasus (Marutta → Adopted Dushyanta → Pandya, Kerala & Chola)
nodes.role: Northwest (Gandhara/Central Asia) & South Indian (Tamil) Aila Bridges
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 108, 144, 146
nodes.notes: Druhyu's descendant Gandhara gave his name to Gandhara (NW Pakistan/Afghanistan); Pracetas's 100 sons migrated north beyond the Himalayas into mleccha lands! Turvasu's line merged into the Pauravas via Marutta's adoption of Dushyanta, with southern Puranic tradition deriving Pandya, Kerala, and Chola from it.

nodes.name: Anavas (Anu's Two Empires): NW Panjab (Ushinara → King Shibi → Kekaya, Madra, Sauvira) & East Bihar (Titikshu → Bali → Anga, Vanga, Kalinga, Pundra, Suhma → Lomapada → King Karna!)
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 108-109, 145-149
nodes.notes: Mahamanas split the Anavas: Ushinara -> famously compassionate King Shibi (and Kekaya/Madra, mothers of Bharata & Nakula/Sahadeva!); Titikshu -> King Bali -> 5 sons founding Anga, Vanga (Bengal!), Kalinga (Odisha!), Pundra & Suhma -> Lomapada (friend of Dasharatha) -> Mahabharata hero Karna -> Vrishasena!

nodes.name: North & South Panchalas (Ajamidha → Nila & Brihadvasu): Mudgala → Divodasa (Atithigva) → King Sudas (Battle of the Ten Kings!) → Drupada → Draupadi & Dhrishtadyumna (+ Drona & Ashvatthama)
nodes.role: Rigvedic Battle of Ten Kings Hero Sudas & Panchala Allies of the Pandavas
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 115-117, 146-148
nodes.notes: Ajamidha's son Nila founded North Panchala (Ahicchattra): Bhrmyashva's 5 sons ('Panchalas') -> Mudgala -> Vadhryashva -> Divodasa (sister Ahalya!) -> King Sudas (victor of the Rigvedic Dasharajna / Battle of Ten Kings against Samvarana & the Ten Tribes!) -> Drupada (father of Draupadi & Dhrishtadyumna, rival of Guru Drona!).

nodes.name: Cedi & Magadha (Kuru → Sudhanvan → Vasu Uparichara): Brihadratha → Jarasandha → Sahadeva → Somadhi (Magadha) & Damaghosha → Shishupala (Cedi)
nodes.role: First Historical Dynasty of Magadha (Barhadrathas) & Cedi
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 118-119, 149
nodes.notes: Kuru's son Sudhanvan's descendant Emperor Vasu Caidyoparichara conquered Cedi & Magadha; his eldest son Brihadratha founded the Barhadratha Dynasty of Magadha -> Emperor Jarasandha (slain by Bhima!) -> Sahadeva -> Somadhi (start of the 22 post-battle Barhadratha kings!).

nodes.name: Post-Mahabharata Kurus (Gens 96–105+): Parikshit II → Janamejaya III → Shatanika → Adhisimakrishna (c. 850 BCE) → Nicakshu (Moved Capital to Kaushambi!) → King Udayana of Vatsa
nodes.era: c. 950-500 BCE (Pargiter Ch. XXIV p. 285; Ch. XXVII p. 330)
nodes.role: Continuation of the Pandava/Kuru Royal Line After Hastinapura Flood
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 285, 330
nodes.notes: When the Ganges washed away Hastinapura c. 820 BCE, Arjuna's 6th-generation descendant Nicakshu moved the Kuru capital to Kaushambi in Vatsa — culminating in famed King Udayana of Vatsa, contemporary of Gautama Buddha!

nodes.name: Bhargavas (Bhrigu → Shukra, Cyavana, Urva → Richika → Jamadagni → Parashurama, Valmiki) & Angirasas (Atharvan → Brihaspati → Bharadvaja → Drona → Ashvatthama; Dirghatamas → Gautama → Kripa; Kanvas)
nodes.role: Complete Genealogies of the Bhargava, Angirasa & Kanva Seers
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 191-202, 218-227
nodes.notes: Synchronizes every great Vedic & Epic sage with the 95-generation royal table: Cyavana (Gen 2), Shukra (Gen 5), Richika/Jamadagni/Parashurama (Gens 31-33), Atharvan/Brihaspati/Dirghatamas/Bharadvaja (Gens 38-41), Valmiki (Gen 64, author of Ramayana!), and Bharadvaja -> Guru Drona -> Ashvatthama (Gens 92-94).

nodes.name: Vasishthas (Vasishtha → Shakti → Parashara → Vyasa → Shuka), Atreyas (Datta & Durvasas), Kashyapas (Kanva, Rishyashringa) & Agastya (+ Lopamudra)
nodes.era: Gens 1-94 (Pargiter Ch. XVIII, XX, XXII, pp. 203-242)
nodes.role: Complete Pedigrees of Vyasa, Durvasas, Rishyashringa & Agastya
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 203-242
nodes.notes: Traces the genuine Vasishtha pedigree (Gen 68 Vasishtha with Sudas -> Shakti -> Parashara -> Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasa [Gen 92, compiler of Vedas & Mahabharata!] -> Shuka), Atreya sages Datta & Durvasas (Gen 31), Kashyapa foster-father Kanva (of Shakuntala) & Rishyashringa, and Agastya (+ Lopamudra of Vidarbha, Gen 42).

nodes.name: Historical Magadha Empires: Barhadrathas (22 Kings) → Pradyotas (5 Kings) → Haryanka/Shishunaga (King Bimbisara & Ajatashatru — Patrons of Buddha!) → 9 Nandas (Mahapadma Nanda)
nodes.role: Bridge from Mahabharata Magadha to Buddha, Alexander & Chandragupta Maurya
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 179-182, 286-287
nodes.notes: Pargiter's critical chronology: 22 Barhadrathas (c. 950-619 BCE) -> 5 Pradyotas -> Shishunaga/Haryanka (Bimbisara & Ajatashatru, contemporaries of Buddha c. 487 BCE!) -> Mahapadma Nanda & 8 sons (exterminated all 10 ancient Kshatriya kingdoms c. 382 BCE, creating the vast empire seized by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE!).

nodes.name: Gupta Empire (Golden Age of India): Sri Gupta → Chandragupta I (+ Kumaradevi Licchavi) → Samudragupta → Chandragupta II Vikramaditya → Kumaragupta I → Skandagupta
nodes.role: Classical Golden Age of Sanskrit, Astronomy (Aryabhata) & Nalanda
nodes.notes: Chandragupta I married Licchavi princess Kumaradevi (of ancient Vaisali!), launching India's Golden Age under Samudragupta & Chandragupta II Vikramaditya (court of Kalidasa!).

nodes.name: Complete Xia Dynasty (All 17 Kings, Bamboo Books): Yu → Qi → Tai Kang → Zhong Kang → Xiang → Shao Kang → Zhu → Huai → Mang → Xie → Bu Jiang → Jiong → Jin → Kong Jia → Gao → Fa → Jie
nodes.era: c. 1989-1557 BCE (Bamboo Books Part III; Shoo King)
nodes.role: First Hereditary Dynasty of China (17 Kings, 432-471 yrs)
sources: Legge Chinese Classics Vol. III (Proleg. pp. 117-127; Shoo pp. 160-171)
nodes.notes: Complete father-son & brother succession from Yu the Great (son of Gun) through the usurpation of Hou Yi & Han Zhuo, restoration by posthumous son Shao Kang (+ Empress Min), 59-yr reign of Bu Jiang, and final tyrant Jie (overthrown by Tang of Shang).

nodes.name: Complete Shang / Yin Dynasty (All 30 Kings, Bamboo Books): Tang → Tai Jia → Tai Wu → Zu Yi → Pan Geng → Wu Ding → Zu Jia → Wen Ding → Di Yi → Di Xin (King Zhou)
nodes.era: c. 1557-1049 BCE (Bamboo Books Part IV; Shoo King)
nodes.role: Oracle-Bone Bronze Age Dynasty (30 Kings Including Tang, Pan Geng & Wu Ding)
sources: Legge Chinese Classics Vol. III (Proleg. pp. 128-141; Shoo pp. 193-278)
nodes.notes: Descended from Emperor Ku & Jiandi -> Xie (13 generations to Tang the Victorious). Features lateral brother-to-brother succession (e.g., 4 brothers Yang Jia -> Pan Geng -> Xiao Xin -> Xiao Yi!), Pan Geng's move to Yin, Wu Ding's 59-yr golden age, and Di Xin's fall at Muye to King Wu of Zhou.

nodes.name: Complete Zhou Dynasty (All 34 Kings, Bamboo Books): Pre-Dynastic (Hou Ji → Danfu → King Wen) → 12 Western Zhou (King Wu → Cheng → Kang → Mu → Li → Xuan → You) → 22 Eastern Zhou (King Ping → King Nan)
nodes.era: 1049-256 BCE (Bamboo Books Part V, Proleg. pp. 142-183)
nodes.role: Longest Dynasty in Chinese History (Mandate of Heaven, Spring & Autumn, Warring States)
sources: Legge Chinese Classics Vol. III (Proleg. pp. 142-183)
nodes.notes: From Emperor Ku & Jiang Yuan -> Hou Ji -> Gong Liu -> Old Duke Danfu (King Tai) -> Jili -> King Wen -> King Wu & Duke of Zhou -> 12 Western Zhou kings (ending when King You fell in 771 BCE) -> 22 Eastern Zhou kings at Luoyang (Ping through King Nan, era of Confucius & Laozi!).

nodes.name: Imperial China Dynastic Bridges: Han Dynasty (Liu Bang / Gaozu → Emperor Wu / Han Wudi; Sima Qian) & Tang Dynasty (Li Yuan → Taizong → Empress Wu Zetian)
nodes.role: Classical Imperial Silk Road Dynasties Connecting China to Parthia, India & Rome
nodes.notes: Han Gaozu (Liu Bang) founded the 400-year Han Dynasty; Han Wudi opened the Silk Road via Zhang Qian to Fergana/Bactria/Parthia (and court historian Sima Qian wrote the Shiji!). Tang Taizong & Wu Zetian presided over cosmopolitan Chang'an.

Izanagi & Izanami. Five Earthly Generations descend from Amaterasu & Taka-mi-musubi via Ninigi (+ Kono-hana-saku-ya-hime) & Hiko-hoho-demi (+ Sea-Princess Toyo-tama-hime) to Jimmu!

nodes.name: 1. Börte Čino ('Blue-Grey Wolf') & Qo'ai Maral ('Fallow Doe')
nodes.role: Heaven-Ordained Ancestors of the Mongol Borjigin Lineage
sources: The Secret History of the Mongols (Rachewiltz)
nodes.notes: Crossed the Tenggis Sea to Burqan Qaldun at the headwaters of the Onan River (Secret History of the Mongols §1, Rachewiltz p. 1).

nodes.name: 2–11. Batačiqan → Tamača → Qoričar Mergen → A'ujam Boro'ul → Sali Qača'u → Yeke Nidün → Sem Soči → Qarču → Borjigidai Mergen → Toroqoljin Bayan
nodes.role: Ten Ancestral Generations from Börte Čino to Dobun Mergen
sources: The Secret History of the Mongols (Rachewiltz)
nodes.notes: Borjigidai Mergen (+ Mongqoljin Qo'a) -> Toroqoljin Bayan (+ Boroqčin Qo'a), father of Du'a Soqor (Dörben clan) and Dobun Mergen.

nodes.name: 12–13. Dobun Mergen & Lady Alan Qo'a → Five Sons (Bügünütei, Belgünütei, Buqu Qatagi, Buqatu Salji & Bodončar Mungqaq)
nodes.role: The Five Arrows Parable & Founder of the Borjigin Royal Clan
sources: The Secret History of the Mongols (Rachewiltz)
nodes.notes: Alan Qo'a (of Qori Tumat) taught her five sons unity using the famous parable of the five arrows. Her youngest son Bodončar Mungqaq (conceived by a radiant golden light!) founded the Borjigin clan — while his stepson Jajiradai became ancestor of Genghis Khan's blood-brother & rival Jamuqa!

nodes.name: 14–18. Qabiči Ba'atur → Menen Tudun (7 Sons incl. Barulas!) → Qači Külük → Qaidu → Bai Šingqor Doqšin → Tumbinai Sečen → Qabul Qa'an (1st All-Mongol Qan!) & Ambaqai Qa'an → Bartan Ba'atur
nodes.role: Khamag Mongol Khagans & Founder of the Barlas Clan (Ancestors of Timur!)
sources: The Secret History of the Mongols (Rachewiltz)
nodes.notes: Menen Tudun's sons Qači'u/Qačula founded the Barulas (Barlas) clan — later ancestors of Timur (Tamerlane) and the Mughal Emperors! Qabul Qa'an became 1st Khan of All Mongols; his sons included Qutula Qa'an and Bartan Ba'atur.

nodes.name: 19. Yisügei Ba'atur & Lady Hö'elün (Olqunu'ut) → Temüjin, Qasar, Qači'un, Temüge, Temülün (+ Bekter & Belgütei)
sources: The Secret History of the Mongols (Rachewiltz)
nodes.notes: Yisügei Ba'atur (poisoned by Tatars when Temüjin was 9) & fierce mother Lady Hö'elün raised Temüjin (born clutching a blood clot at Deli'ün Boldaq!), brothers Joči Qasar, Qači'un, Temüge Otčigin, sister Temülün, and half-brothers Bekter & Belgütei (by Mother Sučigil).

nodes.name: 20. Temüjin / Činggis Qa'an (Genghis Khan, 1162–1227) & Empress Börte (Onggirat)
nodes.role: Founder of the Mongol Empire (Largest Contiguous Land Empire in History)
sources: The Secret History of the Mongols (Rachewiltz)
nodes.notes: Unified the Steppe in 1206 CE as Činggis Qa'an. With principal wife Lady Börte (plus Yisüi, Yisügen, Qulan & Ibaqa Beki) fathered the 4 Great Imperial Sons (Jöči, Ča'adai, Ögödei, Tolui) and 5 diplomat daughters (Qojin, Al Altun, Čečeyigen, Alaqa, Tümelün).

nodes.name: 21–22. The Four Great Houses: Jöči (→ Batu Khan, Golden Horde), Ča'adai (→ Büri), Ögödei Qa'an (+ Töregene → Güyük) & Tolui (+ Sorqaqtani Beki → Möngke Qa'an, Qubilai Qa'an / Kublai Khan & Hülegü Khan)
nodes.role: Great Khans of the Golden Horde, Chagatai, Yuan China & Ilkhanate Persia
sources: The Secret History of the Mongols (Rachewiltz)
nodes.notes: Tolui & Kereyit Christian princess Sorqaqtani Beki produced Möngke (4th Great Khan), Kublai Khan (founder of China's Yuan Dynasty, host of Marco Polo!), and Hülegü (founder of the Persian Ilkhanate). Jöči's son Batu founded the Golden Horde; Ögödei & Güyük ruled Karakorum!

nodes.name: Irish Universal Pedigree: Noah → Japheth → Magog → Fathacht → Sera → Agnomain → Nemed (Ancestor of Fir Bolg, Britons & Tuatha Dé Danann!)
nodes.era: Mythic Irish Settlements (Lebor Gabála Érenn R1 ¶316, p. 127)
nodes.role: Bridge Uniting Genesis 10 (Magog) to Ireland's Pre-Milesian Peoples
sources: Lebor Gabála Érenn Part IV (Macalister ¶280, ¶316, pp. 9, 127)
nodes.notes: Macalister R1 ¶316 traces Nemed directly from Noah -> Japheth -> Magog -> Fathacht -> Braimend -> Esru -> Sru -> Sera -> Tat -> Pamp -> Agnomain -> Nemed! Nemed's surviving branches produced the Fir Bolg (via Starn -> Semeon -> Dela), the Britons (Britán Máel), and the Tuatha Dé Danann (via Iarbonel the Soothsayer -> Bethach -> Tat)!

nodes.name: Complete Fir Bolg Dynasty (Dela's 5 Sons & All 9 Kings): Sláine, Rudraige, Gann, Genann, Sengann → Fiacha → Rindail → Fodbgenid → Eochu mac Eirc (+ Queen Tailtiu)
nodes.era: Pre-Tuatha Dé Ireland (Lebor Gabála Part IV Sect. VI, pp. 7-21)
nodes.role: First Organizers of Ireland's Five Provinces & Tailteann Games
sources: Lebor Gabála Érenn Part IV (Macalister ¶278-289, pp. 7-21)
nodes.notes: Dela's 5 sons & 5 wives (Sláine+Fuat, Gann+Etar, Sengann+Anust, Genann+Cnucha, Rudraige+Liber) divided Ireland into its 5 provinces (Cóiceda). Last king Eochu mac Eirc married Spanish princess Tailtiu (foster-mother of Lugh!) before falling at 1st Battle of Mag Tuired.

nodes.name: Tuatha Dé Danann Line A & B1: Nuadu Airgetlám ('Silver Hand'), Midir & Esarg's 4 Sons (Goibniu, Creidne, Luichtne & Dian Cécht → Cian + Ethniu → Lugh Lámfada!)
nodes.era: Battle of Mag Tuired (Lebor Gabála Part IV Sect. VII, pp. 113-159)
nodes.role: Silver-Handed King Nuadu, Divine Craftsmen & Hero-King Lugh Lámfada
sources: Lebor Gabála Érenn Part IV (Macalister ¶310-316, ¶341, pp. 113-159)
nodes.notes: Nuadu Airgetlám ruled 27 yrs after healer Dian Cécht & Creidne forged his silver hand. Dian Cécht's son Cian married Ethniu (daughter of Fomorian King Balor of the Evil Eye!), fathering Lugh Lámfada ('Long-Arm', master of all arts!), who slew grandfather Balor at 2nd Mag Tuired and reigned 40 yrs!

nodes.name: Tuatha Dé Danann Line B2 (Elada's Sons): The Dagda (Eochu Ollathair → Óengus Mac Óc, Brigit & Cermait → Mac Cuill/Mac Cécht/Mac Gréine) & Ogma (→ Delbaeth → Ériu, Banba, Fódla & 3 Sons of Danu)
nodes.era: Tuatha Dé Danann Golden Age (Lebor Gabála Part IV Sect. VII, pp. 121-197)
nodes.role: The Great Dagda, Goddess Brigit, Ogma & Eponymous Queens of Ireland
sources: Lebor Gabála Érenn Part IV (Macalister ¶313-317, ¶335-344, pp. 121-197)
nodes.notes: Elada fathered Eochu Ollathair (The Great Dagda, reigned 80 yrs -> Óengus Mac Óc, poetess-goddess Brigit, and Cermait -> joint kings Mac Cuill, Mac Cécht, Mac Gréine), Ogma (inventor of Ogham -> Delbaeth -> Fiachna -> Ériu [Ireland!], Banba & Fódla, plus the 3 Gods of Danann: Brian, Iuchar, Iucharba), and Bres (half-Fomorian king)!
